I’m not that big on ai. But I often try these apps out of amusement. For any of those who enjoy this however, here are some key points about it. 
1. No ads. (At least I haven’t encountered any) 
2. You get a LOT out of the free content, with 1 in consideration. Makes you wonder where they get the money…
3. Monetization isn’t really pushed into your face. Which is pretty good compared to many apps these days…
4. The response time is actually pretty fast
5. The actual paid stuff seems like a pretty good deal. Tho I haven’t spent any since I’m a mtg player (financially irresponsible)

*bonus?* it also allows for more mature themes which is nice I guess.

Over all, a more enjoyable waste of time than other apps. You should probably choose this app over other ai apps.

reviews.title: Good story making
reviews.text:
I enjoy AI Dungeon. Great ai options and can make broad amount of stories. There’s a lot of pros, but there are some cons. I find that models LOVE to repeat themselves a LOT. So you have to keep retrying multiple times to get the ai to snap out of the loophole of death. I know AI is not perfect, but i do hope it will have longer memory and have longer thinking so the repeating is minimal. 

Update 9/29/26
The developers are absolutely improving this app each week. They added back Narration which is one of the downsides I missed. They added it back and I love the new features they are doing. 

THE REPETITIVE LOOPING is getting A LOT more rare now. They are increasing the stability of the stories. A company that listens to their customers. 

Pros:
• Great AI models to choose from and a vast selection of modifiers. 
• Great community made stories. 
• What you do in the story matters, a change of action affects the outcome of the story.
• Some AI models put in great details. 
• you can create your own story. 
• You can alter the plot in the middle of a story
• You can add your own characters, and add or remove them during the story. 
• Quick responses. 

Cons
• AI can loop sections in stories (seems like they’re trying to fix this issues with the updates). 
• Sometimes, you have to force close and open the app again, due to when launching a story, it can get stuck on loading story. 
• AI  can sometimes forget earlier parts of the story, which can alter the whole plot of the story.
• You cannot see past a certain amount of story history. 

Overall, a great app that I have been addicted to. Been a subscription supporter for at least a year or so maybe  less. Great fun app when bored. 9.5/10

reviews.title: A Lifechanger
reviews.text:
I’ve been using AI Dungeon since late July, and I genuinely didn’t expect it to mean as much to me as it does.

I’m a writer. Or, more accurately, I was a writer for a very long time. I wrote constantly when I was younger, then life happened, and somewhere along the way I stopped. For roughly fifteen years, writing became something I remembered that I used to do rather than something I actually did.

AI Dungeon changed that.

What I love about it isn’t simply that it can generate prose. There are plenty of tools that can do that. What makes AI Dungeon special is the feeling of playing with a story rather than simply consuming one. I can throw a character into a situation with almost no idea where it’s going, make one strange decision, and watch the world build itself around that decision. Sometimes I have a plan. Sometimes I absolutely do not. Sometimes a completely ridiculous detail becomes important three hundred actions later because the story somehow grew around it.

That unpredictability is the magic.

I’ve built stories involving demons, goblins, boarding schools, spaceships, supernatural nonsense, old gods, murder, philosophy, and at least one purple-and-green goblin whose general philosophy seems to be that reality is more of a suggestion. I’ve also spent an embarrassing amount of time arguing with the AI when it tries to kill characters who very much are not supposed to be dead.

But somewhere in all of that, I started writing again.

Not “AI wrote something and I read it.” I wrote again. I make the choices. I establish the voice. I decide what matters. The AI gives me something to push against, react to, contradict, expand, or occasionally stare at in disbelief. It feels less like outsourcing creativity and more like having an infinitely patient improv partner who has occasionally wandered into the wrong genre.

And that has been unexpectedly meaningful to me.

AI Dungeon gave me a way back into something I thought I had lost. It reminded me that writing doesn’t have to begin with a blank page, a perfect premise, or some grand literary ambition. Sometimes it can begin with “well, that’s weird,” and go from there.

I’ve spent a lot of time in this app, and I suspect I’m going to spend a lot more.

Thank you to everyone who built it.

Update2026:
My kids and I love this app, it’s assisting my youngest learn to read by allowing us to create interactive, choose your own adventure stories. The AI could use minor adjustments, but the new features help it stay on pace with the story, for the most part. It can start showing its cracks on longer stories, but it’s pretty good for short scenarios/stories.

I understand that when we pay for a subscription we get credits to use towards increasing the context length, and you generally get boost anyways but i feel like there should be more benefits! 

I pay for mythic and get a lot of credits but no matter what… the ai models always eat up story memory like no other and when you want to build a stronger world, you can’t because the context length will inevitably fill up faster because of the amount of story cards fighting each other for the output. I just wish i had more benefits other than credit usage. Yeah, i do buy more credits when i run out, but i feel like for the amount im paying for, i am getting what i payed for… right?

reviews.title: Greatly Improved Over The Years
reviews.text:
The app has improved so greatly over the years that it’s became the premiere example of the power of AI in story telling and entertainment. The recent push towards more consistent updates and QOL features like directing the AI towards a story direction is phenomenal. My only complaint is that there’s very little reward to making creations, and there is a clear bias towards NSFW creators and content. 

I’d love to see NSFW toned down, and top creators be rewarded to some degree with either credits or membership being comped due to providing content.

reviews.title: The only “really” good one of its kind.
reviews.text: As much as we jam AI into so many other facets of our lives, a text adventure game seems to be the best application of it as it is. A platform really accessible for free users has allowed me to dig deep into what makes LLM‘ tick. The platform is ever expanding and has really active developers who are quick to bring users into the fold. Free usage means higher prices for paid tiers, barring access from some AI models that someone would actually consider competent. But as much as you could basically do this but better on any standard chat bot, AI Dungeon allows unrestricted and deeply customizable experiences.

reviews.title: Insanely good

reviews.title: The woe of Ai
reviews.text: Generative content gets it wrong, forgets, rewrites or hallucinates. These pitfalls exist here. The story and setting generator and responses can feel alright but it eventually falls apart. Like sand slipping through your fingers. Sad, empty, but useful for inspiration. Use this app while understanding what it is. It is something that will fade away in time. As disheartening as that reality may be.

reviews.title: Good but needs work
reviews.text: This app is really fun and could bring about a whole new genre of gameplay, however it’s not perfect. The AI can have terrible memory and worst of all it’ll bring in some weird details and have characters do things that make no sense. It’s possible to correct the AI but I shouldn’t have to do that in the first place, I also noticed that it makes grammatical errors too, something I never thought I’d see in an app that relies on AI.
